text.en:
At the port of Muziris a ship waited to be loaded with sacks of pepper. Traders came from distant lands to buy it.
"Our spices are known across the sea," said the port officer proudly.

In the far south three kingdoms were famous: the Cheras in the west with Vanji, the Cholas in the Kaveri delta with Uraiyur and later Puhar, and the Pandyas in the south with Madurai. They are known as the three crowned kings (Muventar).
Their ports traded pepper, pearls, cotton cloth, ivory and gems with Rome, Southeast Asia and other lands, and Roman coins have been found in the south. Sangam literature, poems in Tamil, describes their kings, battles, trade and daily life.
Later dynasties such as the Pallavas built great temples at Mamallapuram and Kanchipuram. Reorganisation of states and the growth of local rulers shaped this period.
The three ancient Tamil kingdoms were the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas.
The Pandyas ruled from Madurai. The Cholas ruled the Kaveri delta.
Their ports traded pepper, pearls and cotton cloth with distant lands.
Sangam poems tell us about their kings and daily life.

problem.en: How do we know that South India traded with Rome?

text.en: Roman gold coins have been found in the south.
Sangam poems also describe foreign traders at the ports.
So both objects and writings show the trade.

prompt.en: A friend says Tamil Nadu had only one kingdom in ancient times. How will you correct this?

requiredIdeas.en: There were three: the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas.

points.en: The Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas were the three ancient Tamil kingdoms.
Their ports traded with Rome and Southeast Asia.
